steady_state_tone_three_point.why: replacing white noise with a pure tone at the measured |H| peak (322 Hz): a tone puts all its energy in one bin, so the microphone band level sits about 40 dB above the room floor instead of under it. Three points, same source level (0.15 FS), same gain -8 dB and hp volume 40, candidate model loaded in all three.
steady_state_tone_three_point.open: digital gain forced to 0: microphone 322 Hz 45.44 dB, mic RMS -24.6 dBFS, peak -16.0
steady_state_tone_three_point.bypass: loop closed, candidate coefficients loaded but not subtracted: 322 Hz 49.19 dB (+3.75 dB vs open)
steady_state_tone_three_point.cancel: loop closed, subtraction active: 322 Hz 44.43 dB
steady_state_tone_three_point.acoustic_result: microphone at 322 Hz is 4.76 dB lower in cancel than in bypass, and 1.01 dB lower than with no loop at all: the canceller removes the loop's +3.75 dB boost and slightly more
steady_state_tone_three_point.all_arms: bit_exact=true, wide_residual_frames=0, bit22=0, no gain/mix/prediction/residual saturation, no clipping, completed
steady_state_tone_three_point.limits: one frequency, one level, small-signal (loop only +3.75 dB above the no-loop path). This is a cancellation depth at 322 Hz, NOT ASG and NOT the maximum achievable
steady_state_tone_three_point.meaning: first steady-state measurement this session that clears the noise floor. Quote the three numbers separately: CD(322) = 6.37 dB (model fit), loop boost = 3.75 dB (audible-benefit scale), acoustic difference = 4.76 dB (= 3.75 + 1.01 overshoot, not the benefit). Single frequency, single level: not ASG. White-noise band shares gave +1.6 / -4.7 / -2.1 dB with a flipping sign and are unusable.
steady_state_tone_three_point.cancellation_depth_is: CD(322), residual depth between the bypass and cancel arms: the quantity the cancel branch minimises. MODEL FIT, not a benefit. See reporting_split_v3_working_point.
steady_state_tone_three_point.loop_boost_is: bypass microphone 49.19 minus open microphone 45.44: what the closed loop adds in that band, and therefore the most a canceller can recover there. This is the audible-benefit scale.
steady_state_tone_three_point.acoustic_difference_is: bypass microphone minus cancel microphone = loop boost 3.75 + overshoot 1.01. Quoting 4.76 as a benefit overstates it; quote 3.75.

listener_two_arm_2026_10_28.reading: the microphone level drops 5.6 dB with cancellation active, but the person doing the speaking cannot hear that as a loudness difference. The likely reason is methodological: the talker is also the listener, so their own direct voice (bone conduction plus direct sound) dominates what they hear, and a change in the played level is masked. The historical sessions used a separate listener 20 cm from the speaker for exactly this reason.
listener_two_arm_2026_10_28.what_it_does_not_say: it does NOT say the cancellation is inaudible; it says this listener position cannot resolve it. A separate listener at the speaker, or a recorded A/B of the played signal, is needed to answer the audible-benefit question.

unit_fix_2026_10_28.error: level_dbfs took the peak bin of the Hann-windowed spectrum without dividing by the window coherent gain, so every absolute level was inflated by 20*log10(N/4) (about 60 dB at N=4096). A 0.25 full-scale tone read +48.16 dBFS instead of -12.04 dBFS.
unit_fix_2026_10_28.fix: amplitude = 2*|rfft(x*win)| / sum(win); level = 20*log10(amplitude). Verified: a synthetic 0.25 full-scale tone now reads -12.04 dBFS (test_tone_round_guard.py, 17 checks).
unit_fix_2026_10_28.effect_on_conclusions: NONE on the three-point quantities: all three signals pass through the same window, so CD(322), loop boost, acoustic difference and overshoot are unchanged (8.43 / 4.24 / 5.45 / 1.21 dB). Only the absolute levels were wrong and are now in real dBFS.

audible_benefit_claim_retracted_2026_10_.retracted_claim: the played output was too quiet (-42..-47 dBFS) and the listener benefit is a measured negative
audible_benefit_claim_retracted_2026_10_.why_invalid: the driver saves the LAST 16384 frames of the ring, i.e. 0.336 s. The alternating run was 2.4 s with a 2.0 s source, so the saved window starts at 2.064 s and ends at 2.400 s - entirely AFTER the source ended. The levels therefore describe the decay tail, not program material, and no loudness statement can be made from them.
audible_benefit_claim_retracted_2026_10_.what_survives: the same-window arm difference (1.91 dB over the four arms, gate excluded; C independently got 1.905 dB) may be kept as a same-window comparison, but it is not a loudness measurement either.
audible_benefit_claim_retracted_2026_10_.what_was_also_wrong: the earlier 1.38 dB summary included the gate run in the zero-arm mean; the four-arm mean is 1.91 dB.
audible_benefit_claim_retracted_2026_10_.correct_method_for_a_real_measurement: the run duration must be no longer than the saved window (0.336 s) so that the capture falls inside the source, or the capture length must be made configurable. Neither was done here, and no new audible trial was spent.
audible_benefit_claim_retracted_2026_10_.consequence_for_the_freeze: the audible-benefit question is OPEN again: it is neither a measured negative nor a measured positive. What stands is the 322 Hz three-point verdict (cancellation_holds) and every listener record as a record.

coupling_table.how: IN-PHASE UPPER BOUND ONLY: 1/(1-g*|H|) assumes the loop adds in phase. The measured value at -8 dB is +3.75 dB, not +9.39. Do not use this table to predict loudness; B derived a phase of about 39.8 degrees at 322 Hz, and the real curve peaks near g = -6.7 dB at +3.87 dB, with -8 dB only 0.12 dB below that peak.

consequences: raising g cannot buy loudness on the zero arm: played/source = 1/|1-gH| runs -14 -> +2.21, -10 -> +3.29, -8 -> +3.75, -6.7 -> +3.87 (peak), -6 -> +3.83; -8 dB is 0.12 dB from the maximum
-4 dB is above the bypass critical gain (-4.40 dB), so it self-oscillates with no cancellation at all
what is left of the loudness gap is speaker efficiency, directivity and distance to the listener, which g cannot fix

whether the CANDIDATE can go louder is unknown: played/source = 1/|1-g(H-Hhat)| needs the phase of H-Hhat, and offline data only has per-point magnitudes (max 0.9247). Report only "stability margin 5.08 dB higher than the zero arm (a bound difference, not a measured ASG)"
clipping follows speech effort, not distance: both 12 cm and 20 cm produced bit22=1

correction_to_B_option_2.B_said: lowering the Codec ADC gain by k equals lowering g, so it is wasted effort
correction_to_B_option_2.why_that_is_incomplete: it is a headroom move, not a gain move. Scaling the ADC by k and the coefficients by k, then the digital gain by 1/k, gives out = (g/k)(k*m - k*p) = g*(m - p): identical loop gain and identical playback level, but the microphone path no longer saturates. The coefficient scaling is exact (B says so himself), so no refit is needed. The point is to stop destroying input information at 12 cm, which no digital stage can undo.
correction_to_B_option_2.cost: identity has to be re-registered (scaled coefficients) and the ADC gain is a calibrated parameter

the bypass arm microphone is 4.76 dB higher than the cancel arm at the same speech level, so bypass reaches the rail first. That is the cost of that arm, not a failure; record it separately

reporting_split_v3_working_point.source: B 86061a7, adopted by A 2026-10-28; three quantities must never be quoted interchangeably

cd_322_db.what: residual depth at 322 Hz: bypass residual vs cancel residual. It is what the cancel branch minimises and it measures model fit.

loop_boost_db.what: bypass microphone (49.19) minus open microphone (45.44): how much the closed loop raises that band, so it is also the most a canceller can recover there

acoustic_difference_db.what: bypass microphone (49.19) minus cancel microphone (44.43) = loop boost 3.75 + cancel overshoot 1.01
acoustic_difference_db.not: not the benefit: quoting 4.76 as benefit overstates it by the 1.01 overshoot

phase_of_H_at_322_derived_by_B.consequence: g plus |H| in dB is an amplitude bound only; it cannot predict loudness. An in-phase assumption would have predicted 9.4 dB where 3.75 dB was measured, and the 5.7 dB gap is entirely phase.

codec_unmute_pop_fix.symptom: the operator heard a "du" from the speaker; the microphone hit the ADC rail for a few milliseconds at the very first frames of a run, so the input-full-scale stop fired before any program material arrived. Three consecutive gate attempts stopped after 5 / 650 / 114 frames with 5-87 samples at the rail while the room was otherwise quiet.
codec_unmute_pop_fix.root_cause: the driver unmuted the codec and armed the run in the same instant, so the unmute pop landed inside the first captured frames.
codec_unmute_pop_fix.fix: CODEC_SETTLE_SECONDS = 0.25 between the codec unmute and the arm, so the pop decays BEFORE the counters start. No threshold moved and no protection was relaxed: the arm point moved, the protection is exactly as strict as before.
codec_unmute_pop_fix.verification: after the fix the same tone round and the same 60 s run completed with bit22=0 and no rail samples; the clap still stops the run with input_clip.
